title: ASPICE
description: Automotive SPICE: process reference and assessment model, capability levels, VDA scope.

questions.question: Who publishes Automotive SPICE?

answers.text: VDA QMC (Quality Management Center of the German automotive industry association)

questions.explanation: Automotive SPICE is owned and published by the VDA QMC. ISO 26262 is functional safety, a separate standard.

questions.question: Which measurement framework does Automotive SPICE 3.1 use for rating process capability?
questions.explanation: ASPICE 3.1 is conformant with ISO/IEC 33004 and uses the measurement framework of ISO/IEC 33020 (predecessor: ISO/IEC 15504).

questions.question: What is the name of capability level 3?
questions.explanation: Levels: 0 Incomplete, 1 Performed, 2 Managed, 3 Established, 4 Predictable, 5 Innovating. 'Optimizing' is CMMI wording.

questions.question: Which percentage range corresponds to the rating 'Largely achieved' (L)?
Which ratings are required for a process to reach capability level 2?

answers.text: PA 2.1 and PA 2.2 rated at least Largely achieved
PA 3.1 rated at least Partially achieved

questions.explanation: A level is reached if its own attributes are at least L and all lower-level attributes are F.

questions.question: Which processes belong to the VDA scope (formerly HIS scope) in ASPICE 3.1?
questions.explanation: VDA scope 3.1: ACQ.4, MAN.3, SUP.1, SUP.8, SUP.9, SUP.10, SYS.2–SYS.5, SWE.1–SWE.6. SPL.2 is not part of it.

questions.question: In ASPICE 3.1, which process verifies the software requirements defined in SWE.1?

answers.text: SWE.5 Software Integration and Integration Test

questions.explanation: V-model pairs: SWE.1↔SWE.6, SWE.2↔SWE.5, SWE.3↔SWE.4.

questions.question: Which activities belong to SWE.4 Software Unit Verification (ASPICE 3.1)?

answers.text: Static verification of software units, e.g. static analysis or code review
Testing software units against unit verification criteria
Testing the integrated software against software requirements

questions.explanation: SWE.4 covers static and dynamic verification of units. Testing against SW requirements is SWE.6.

questions.question: ASPICE 3.1 distinguishes traceability and consistency. What does consistency add?

answers.text: That linked elements actually match in content, not only that a link exists
Nothing; both terms mean the same
That every requirement has exactly one test case

questions.explanation: Traceability = links exist (bidirectionally). Consistency = the linked items agree in content and are complete.

questions.question: Which process is responsible for baselines and controlled storage of work products?
questions.explanation: SUP.8 identifies configuration items, manages branches and baselines and controls storage and release.

questions.question: Which process attributes belong to capability level 2?
questions.explanation: CL2 = PA 2.1 + PA 2.2. CL3 = PA 3.1 Process definition + PA 3.2 Process deployment.

questions.question: Base practices are indicators for which process attribute?
questions.explanation: Base practices (and output work products) indicate PA 1.1. Generic practices indicate PA 2.1 and above.

questions.question: Which process groups were newly introduced with Automotive SPICE 4.0?
questions.explanation: 4.0 added HWE and MLE (and VAL.1 Validation). Cybersecurity stays in the separate 'Automotive SPICE for Cybersecurity' PAM.

questions.question: What are 'work products' called in Automotive SPICE 4.0?
questions.explanation: 4.0 replaced 'work products' with 'information items' and reworked the indicators.

questions.question: Which intacs assessor grades may lead an Automotive SPICE assessment?
questions.explanation: Provisional assessors may only take part as co-assessors. Lead assessors must be at least Competent.

questions.question: An ASPICE assessment certifies that the product (e.g. the ECU software) is defect-free.
questions.explanation: ASPICE rates process capability of a project or organizational unit, not product quality or safety.

questions.question: For what is a capability level determined in an assessment?

answers.text: Once for the whole project, as an average

questions.explanation: Results are a capability profile: one level per process instance. There is no single 'project level'.

questions.question: Which percentage range corresponds to the rating 'Partially achieved' (P)?
questions.explanation: P means some evidence of a systematic approach exists, but parts are unpredictable.

questions.question: Which process handles requests to change already agreed requirements or work products?
questions.explanation: SUP.10 records, analyzes, approves and tracks change requests. SUP.9 handles problems (defects).

questions.question: Which statements about the 'Plug-in concept' of Automotive SPICE 3.1 are correct?

answers.text: System-level processes (SYS) can be combined with domain processes such as SWE, HWE or MEE
It allows hardware and mechanical engineering to be assessed alongside software
It replaces capability levels with maturity levels

questions.explanation: The plug-in concept connects SYS processes with domain-specific engineering processes. Capability levels stay.
